note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, lighting answer and net answer below comes from the Naperville Park District's own pages: one location page per park, each with a single sentence about pickleball, and its Park It page, which states that the courts at six named parks are outdoor. The operator is the Park District, an Illinois special-purpose local government with its own board, and not the City of Naperville. Where the District is silent, on hours, on price, on parking beyond a label, on lighting at Nike's four dedicated courts, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
The Park District says one thing about parking at each of these three parks, and it is a label. "Parking Spaces" appears in the amenity list of Nike Sports Complex, Ranchview Park and Ashbury Park alike, with no capacity, no fee and no word on when a lot fills.

Nike publishes a parking map as well, and a paved trail there runs north to south with "a connection to the pickleball courts". Restrooms are listed at Nike on a seasonal schedule the District asks you to check. Ranchview and Ashbury list none, which is a silence rather than a no.
slots.peak_hours:
The Park District publishes no hours, no price, no busy periods and no open-play schedule for any of these courts. What it does publish is lighting. Ranchview Park "has 6 unlit courts" and Ashbury Park "has 4 unlit courts", so thirteen of the twenty-five courts here are daylight courts by the operator's own word.

Nike Sports Complex is where the answer splits. The District writes that it "has 4 dedicated pickleball courts and there are 8 lit tennis courts lined for pickleball". The word "lit" attaches to the eight tennis courts and not to the four dedicated ones, so Nike's lighting is recorded here as unknown. Those eight lined courts are the District's stated option after dark. All twenty-five courts are outdoor, and the District points to the Fort Hill Activity Center for indoor play "during an open gym time".
slots.surface_condition:
Ranchview Park is one of very few venues on this site with a stated surface, and the only one whose operator states why. The Park District writes that "The tennis/pickleball courts have a modular plastic tile system to ensure continuous operation and minimize maintenance", and explains that traditional coatings kept failing there because of moisture from the roof of the concrete reservoir below.

What the District distinguishes at every venue is the court itself. Nike has four "dedicated pickleball courts" and eight tennis courts "lined for pickleball"; Ranchview's nine are striping on tennis courts; Ashbury's four are on tennis courts "using tennis nets". Nothing is said about condition, cracks or resurfacing dates.
slots.local_scene:
Twenty-five courts across three Park District parks, all of them outdoor, none of them priced, and thirteen of them stated unlit. Naperville is the first city in Illinois on this site and the first whose operator is a park district rather than a city department: the Naperville Park District owns and runs these parks and publishes their courts, one sentence per park. At every published venue it says something about nets: "participants must provide their own nets" at Nike, "using tennis nets" at Ashbury, and at Ranchview two sentences that disagree, which few operators on this site do at all.

The number this page cannot give is the District's real total. Its Park It page names six parks with outdoor pickleball courts, and three of them are missing here because the addresses the District prints for them do not resolve.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Nike Sports Complex has twelve pickleball courts, the largest count published in Naperville: four dedicated courts and eight tennis courts lined for pickleball, which the Park District describes as lit. Bring a net, because the District states that participants must provide their own. The complex has restrooms on a seasonal schedule, a paved trail that connects to the courts, and its own parking map.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to know what you are standing on
best_for.text: Ranchview Park has nine courts striped onto its tennis courts on a modular plastic tile system, and it is the one venue in Naperville whose surface the Park District states and explains: painted coatings kept failing on the roof of the concrete reservoir beneath. The courts are unlit by the District's own word, and the page says two different things about nets, so bring one.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to turn up with nothing but a paddle
best_for.text: Ashbury Park has four courts on its tennis courts, "using tennis nets" in the Park District's words, so there is a net there when you arrive, a tennis net at tennis height. The courts are unlit, so this is daylight play, with two games running at once at most. The park lists parking spaces, ponds, fishing and a multi-use trail along the shoreline.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Naperville have?
faqs.a: Twenty-five across three Naperville Park District parks: twelve at Nike Sports Complex, nine at Ranchview Park and four at Ashbury Park. The District's own total is larger. It names three more outdoor venues whose printed addresses do not resolve: Wolf's Crossing Community Park with eight courts, DuPage River Sports Complex with four and Frontier Sports Complex with six, plus Knoch Park and the indoor Fort Hill Activity Center, which state no count at all.

Only the eight tennis courts lined for pickleball at Nike Sports Complex, which the District calls "lit". It says nothing about Nike's four dedicated courts. Ranchview Park and Ashbury Park are stated "unlit", so thirteen of the twenty-five courts close with the daylight.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring my own net?
faqs.a: At Nike Sports Complex, yes: "participants must provide their own nets". At Ashbury Park, no: the four courts are "using tennis nets", a tennis net at tennis height. At Ranchview Park the District's page says both "6 unlit courts using tennis nets" and that six courts "on the east side require patrons to bring their own nets", so bring one and you are covered either way.
